text:
marc: heads up — bringing up Harrier21b (v1-int4) on canary pool. initial perf numbers looked promising but seeing OOMs on a subset of pods after ~120s into long generations. logs attached below.

kai: any reproducer? load pattern?

marc: yes repro with conv long-chat tests. config used: `batch_size: 6`, `microbatch: 2`, `max_new_tokens: 512`, `kv_prefetch: true`, `slot_reserve: 0`

anita: can you paste the oom trace?

marc: ```
[2026-03-20T14:12:40Z] OOM: failed allocate 1.2G for attention_kv_cache
process: /opt/redwood/runtime/serve pid=4123 gpu=0
stack: (alloc->evict->alloc)
```

ops-bot: deploy-canary harrier-21b-int4 v1 started by @marc at 2026-03-20T14:10:34Z

kai: looks like memory fragmentation + prefetching is pushing us over. int4 reduces model size but increases allocator churn due to many small allocations for kv cache?

anita: agree. int4 lowers model footprint but fragmentation on long-window gen still spikes. are we using adaptive-windowing?

marc: tested with window 2048, kv chunking default. Also saw periodic GC-ish pauses in the runtime logs.

sophia: quick idea: try enabling `slot_reserve: 0.15` and reduce `max_new_tokens` default to 256 in canary to see if stability improves. Also try disabling `kv_prefetch` — prefetching seems to increase concurrency of allocations.

lucas: +1 to disabling prefetch for int4 canary. we should also test with `batch_size: 4` to lower instantaneous memory pressure.

marc: will push a canary patch: disable kv_prefetch, slot_reserve 0.12, batch_size 4, max_new_tokens 256. rolling now.

ops-bot: canary update harrier-21b-int4 v1.1 rolled to 3 pods at 2026-03-20T14:20:11Z

kai: while that's rolling, let's run a quick eval comparing quality and perf: run ~200 long-chat sessions and capture tail-latency, tokens/s, and regression rate vs v1-int8 baseline.

anita: note: int8 baseline had no OOMs with `batch_size:8` and `max_new_tokens:512` in the same pool. keep that as anchor.

sophia: also run memory defrag metric (allocator external) and KV-slot-utilization to verify fragmentation drop.

marc: results after 30m: new canary stable (no OOMs so far). tail latency +8% (expected from smaller batch), tokens/s -12% on long-gen, but memory fragmentation metric down ~42%.

kai: quality delta?

marc: automated eval on our prompt-set shows negligible regression (0.4% lower in Rouge-L equiv), human spot checks ok.

anita: trade-off looks reasonable. propose: set canary defaults for Harrier21b-int4 to `batch_size:4`, `max_new_tokens:256`, `kv_prefetch:false`, `slot_reserve:0.12`, and enable an automatic fallback to int8 if a pod hits >85% GPU alloc failures in 5m window.

lucas: can we add a metric alert for sudden increase in `alloc_fail_count` and an automated temporary throttle that reduces `max_new_tokens` per-request until steady?

kai: yes — infra can add a policy: on alloc_fail_count > 5 in 5m, set per-route soft cap `max_new_tokens=128` and scale down microbatch concurrency by 50% for that route for 10m.

marc: created PR with canary defaults + fallback policy, request review: https://git.internal/redwood/harrier-onboard/pull/84

sophia: LGTM from ops side. also add note to model card: "int4 unstable for long-window >256 default, prefer int8 for heavy long-chat SLOs"

marc: will schedule a full canary + expanded eval tomorrow. thanks all :thumbsup:
